_comment: The canonical admin URL per Instatic site — the single answer to 'what link do I send?'.
`adminUrl` is the origin a person should work from; `check-origins.mjs` appends its www/apex
twin automatically, so list only what that would not derive: a second client domain, the
platform host, staging, an old domain people still have bookmarked.
List a host even when it is currently broken — a host nobody checks is a host nobody fixes,
and the checker's job is to keep saying so until it is clean.
This file is the claim; `node check-origins.mjs --all` is the proof, and it probes the RUNNING
server rather than the Railway dashboard. Re-run it after any domain change or redeploy and
fix whichever of the two is wrong.
No secrets here. Credentials live in the per-worktree .env and never in this repo.
A `<client>-staging` entry is that client's staging instance; tools/instatic-plugins reads production and staging hosts from here (2026-09-23).
_dns_comment: `dns` records the CNAME target Railway minted for each custom domain, so a change is
detectable. Railway mints a RANDOM target per domain and it is stable for the life of that
domain record — a redeploy does NOT change it. It changes when the domain is deleted and
re-added, which mints a fresh one and silently orphans whatever Cloudflare still points at.
`node check-dns.mjs` compares these against Railway and against public DNS. That one needs
`railway login`, because a Cloudflare-proxied record hides its CNAME from the world and
Railway is the only source of truth for what it should be.
`env` names the Railway environment the domain lives in; omit it for production. A staging
domain is invisible from the production environment, and without this the checker reports it
as unreadable rather than checking it. A `<client>-staging` entry's `railway.environment` does the same for all its hosts.
Update these ONLY after Cloudflare has been fixed — `node check-dns.mjs --record` prints the
current values in this shape. Recording a change without making it just files the outage.

THREE production faults fixed the same day: (1) the `www` Cloudflare record pointed at the APEX's target l6wotb3m and now points at pkez8lkn; (2) the zone's non-US block carried no path condition, so it 403d /.well-known/acme-challenge/ and no certificate could ever issue — it now exempts that path and the staging host, and BOTH production certificates went ISSUE_FAILED -> VALID within minutes of the retry; (3) the apex and www served byte-identical pages with no canonical, and the apex now 301s to www via a Cloudflare dynamic redirect that itself exempts the ACME path. `mason-park.up.railway.app` and `mason-park-production.up.railway.app` no longer exist — both were deleted before this session and 404; the platform host is gone from `alternates`, and INSTATIC_BASE_URL in the Mason Park worktrees now points at www. Staging carries X-Robots-Tag noindex via Cloudflare and emitCanonical:false on its Open Graph plugin.

Now https://brandklout.ai,https://www.brandklout.ai,https://brandklout-production.up.railway.app; redeployed (a127e9f6) and all three verified OK. www is a separate Railway customDomain reading REQUIRES_UPDATE because its CNAME is proxied by Cloudflare; it serves and accepts the login regardless, so it is not listed as an alternate — check-origins appends the www twin itself.

Stood up 2026-09-22 per process 21-instatic-staging-clone. PUBLIC_ORIGIN is the staging host ALONE, set with skipDeploys before anything could deploy, because a duplicated environment is born holding production's list. The Railway service domain it minted (brandklout-staging.up.railway.app) was DELETED: it bypasses Cloudflare, so no edge rule can de-index it. One door only. Cloudflare response-header rule 1d696d05809041c386b3f328ab0265fb sets X-Robots-Tag noindex, nofollow on this host, and emitCanonical is OFF on its Open Graph plugin - noindex plus a canonical at production is the one pairing Google can resolve against production. There is no www twin and there must not be one.
